What simple things do you do to save?
How do you stretch a dollar? Any money saving tips you'd like to share?
My great grandmother once said: Don't focus on how to save. Instead focus on how to make more. If you make more you don't have to worry about how to save.
Interesting. My folks always taught me 'it's not how much you make, it's how much you save'. Very different philosophies.

Trying to save your spending teaches you complacency, you spend all your time worrying about how to cut corners, how to keep your status the way it is and to never excel. Focusing on how to make more is about improvement. How to build your worth, grow your properties, investments, etc.

Now, that's not to say it's a bad idea to not buy off brand cereal because it's cheaper but if you spend an hour a week cutting coupons to save 10 bucks at the grocery store, you could have worked overtime for time and a half and earn 15 dollars (assuming you get paid 10 bucks an hour). You could have cleaned your neighbors gutters for 25 bucks. You could have done something else to earn more than what you would have saved.

EDIT: Now that I think about this, this is probably more apt for /v/traditionalhushands.
Ah, I see what you mean. Good point.

I think the big 3 are something like housing, transportation, and food? Maybe taxes or utilities. So I focus on those first.

  • Don't pay for more housing than you need. (also, big city living in SF or NYC is a huge "luxury" expense you can skip). Bigger house means higher utility, insurance, property tax, and furnishing bills.

  • Don't pay for more car than you need. My cheap car I bought for $7k about 5 years ago is just as good as a brand new Tesla or whatever for getting around.

  • Shop at a cheap store like Aldi for the staples to cut your food bill in half of so. Avoid junk food, and booze to save even more. And cook instead of restaurants for the vast majority of meals of course.

  • For taxes, if you're in the 25% bracket or higher, definitely look into the traditional 401k or IRA to put aside money for later while reducing your tax bill. Putting in $23,500 this year between the 401k and IRA will cut your federal income tax bill by $5,875 if you're firmly in the 25% bracket.

Simple changes on the big things are where you can find the most bang for your buck.

We only drive used cars. My husband knows how to fix them and things he doesn't know how to fix he has some good connections that will give him a good price. This means we spend less on cars and on car ins.

We try to mostly eat at home and I look at sale ads before I menu plan and base my menu off of what is on sale and what we have on hand. I will also buy a lot of discounted foods especially meat and will freeze them or use them in a day or two.

I'm starting my Christmas shopping now for my girls too so it spreads out the expense but also so I can buy clearance things that I see they would like. My mom would do this with birthday gifts for birthday parties we attended. When it was time to go to a party we picked something from the box our friend would like instead of going out and buying something at full price. I've started doing this a little as well.

When ever I need something at Joanne fabrics I know they have coupons on their website so I look there and pull that up before I go.

Pretty much I buy almost everything used, on sale, or clearanced if I can help it.

I grow and freeze a lot of produce, barring exotic fruit, I have it canned or frozen, though I am growing a pineapple and avocado from leftover stems and seeds, I doubt they'll produce, but I like house plants. We live in a rural area so I limit my trips to town to twice a week, during these I visit my gym (YMCA, has classes, pool, sauna, steam room, gym, and weight room, I could cut this expense if need be but the value for our family is worth it), library, and do all my shopping.
